list: The official 55 trophies, as PlayStation publishes them

stages.name: First Days in Leonida
stages.note: Chapter 1, the opening missions, and the habits worth starting on day one.

stages.name: Building the Crew
stages.note: Chapters 2 and 3, the first heists, and the activity types to sample early.

stages.name: Endgame: Chapter 4 and the Finale
stages.note: The last story push. Keep a manual save before the point-of-no-return choices.

stages.name: Strangers, Collectibles and Side Hustles
stages.note: Post-story cleanup: stranger strands, card sets, robberies and one-off moments.

stages.name: The 100 Percent Push and the Platinum
stages.note: The long counters: stunts, shooting-range golds, challenges and full completion.

trophies.guide: The platinum. It lands on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so treat it as the receipt for the whole list rather than a task of its own.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

steps.t: Earn every other trophy on this list; the platinum has no task of its own.
Work the list in roadmap order so the missable-flagged and one-off trophies are banked before the final push.
When the 54th trophy pops, this one follows immediately in the same session.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing the early mission Gone Fishing. It cannot be missed: play the opening hours and it pops at the mission's end card.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

steps.t: Start a new game and follow the opening story beats until the Gone Fishing job is offered.
Play the mission through to its conclusion; there are no optional objectives tied to this trophy.
The trophy pops on the mission-complete screen, before control returns to free roam.
If it ever fails to appear, the mission can be replayed from the story menu without starting over.

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 1 of the story. Pure progression: every chapter trophy in the game is unmissable and awarded in order.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

steps.t: Play the story from the prologue onward, following the marker missions in order.
Complete the chapter's closing mission; the chapter card confirms the finish.
The trophy is awarded as Chapter 2 unlocks on the map.
Side content can be left for later; nothing in Chapter 1 locks away afterwards.

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 2. The chapter where the crew's money-making starts in earnest; the trophy itself is simple story progression.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

steps.t: Continue the story markers after Chapter 1 until the Chapter 2 finale becomes available.
Finish the closing mission of the chapter; expect a longer set-piece than Chapter 1's.
The trophy pops as the chapter-complete card shows and Chapter 3 opens.
Keep a manual save at the chapter break: later choice trophies are easier with clean saves to return to.

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3, the chapter that opens up Vice City proper. Unmissable story progression.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

steps.t: Follow the Chapter 3 story chain from the chapter break save.
Complete the mid-chapter heist setup missions before attempting the finale.
Finish the chapter's final mission; the trophy lands with the chapter card.
New districts and activities unlock here, so sample one of each activity type now for Master of None.

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4, the last full chapter before the endgame. Unmissable, but save before its closing choices.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

steps.t: Make a manual save before starting the chapter's final sequence of missions.
Play the Chapter 4 chain in order; the finale mission is signposted in the mission list.
The trophy pops at the chapter-complete card, ahead of the final mission unlock.
Do the choice-related cleanup (Actions Speak Louder) before pushing into the finale.

trophies.guide: Finish the final story mission. One of only two golds on the list, and the natural end of a first playthrough; the game continues in free roam afterwards for cleanup.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

steps.t: Reach the final mission by completing Chapter 4 and its closing beats.
Save manually before accepting the finale; it is the game's point of no return for story choices.
Play the finale to the credits; the trophy pops as the credits begin.
After the credits you return to free roam with everything else on the list still available.
If a choice in the finale worries you, the pre-finale save lets you see the other branch without a new playthrough.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for the Breakfast Run mission, an early driving job. Unmissable progression.
trophies.name: Trust

steps.t: Pick up the Breakfast Run job from its story marker during the opening chapter.
Drive the route as directed; the mission teaches the wanted-level escape basics on the way.
Finish the delivery to complete the mission and pop the trophy.
The route doubles as an easy early driving practice for the later race trophies.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for The Cartel Heist, the first full heist of the campaign. Approach choices change the route, not the trophy.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

steps.t: Unlock the heist by finishing its setup missions in Chapter 2.
Pick either approach at the planning board; both complete the trophy.
Play the heist through the escape; the trophy pops at the payout screen.
Bank the take afterwards: the laundering and spending trophies build on heist money.
A loud approach earns more police attention but the same trophy; pick the approach you play better.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for the mission Child's Play. Unmissable; awarded at the mission's end regardless of performance.
trophies.name: Family Matters

steps.t: Take the Child's Play mission from its marker when it appears in Chapter 2 or 3.
Follow the mission objectives; there are no fail states tied to the trophy itself.
The trophy pops on the mission-complete screen.
Replay is available from the story menu if you want to see a different outcome.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for Headliners, a late-campaign mission. Unmissable progression toward the finale.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

steps.t: Reach Headliners by following the Chapter 4 story chain.
Complete the mission's set-piece sequence; checkpoints are generous.
The trophy is awarded at the mission-complete card.
Save after this one: the endgame choice trophies sit just past it.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for VCIA Takedown, the airport-authority mission late in the campaign. Unmissable; it also sets up the Catch Me If You Can opportunity at the same airport.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

steps.t: Reach VCIA Takedown in the Chapter 4 mission chain.
Play the takedown through; the airport interior stays open to you afterwards.
The trophy pops at the mission-complete screen.
Remember the airside layout from this mission: Catch Me If You Can is earned at the same airport.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for Operation Savage Glory, one of the last missions before the finale. Unmissable progression.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

steps.t: Start Operation Savage Glory from its marker near the end of Chapter 4.
Complete the operation's objectives in order; the trophy ignores your approach.
It pops on the mission-complete card, just before the finale unlocks.
Make your pre-finale manual save right after this mission.

trophies.guide: Reach a full 100% on the in-game completion counter. This is the list's long pole: story, strands, collectibles and activity quotas all feed the one percentage, so track it in the stats screen and mop up by category.
trophies.name: A Long Road

steps.t: Finish the story first; the counter's biggest single chunk is the campaign and its missions.
Open the stats screen and work the completion categories from the largest missing percentage down.
Clear every stranger strand, collectible set and activity quota the counter lists; partial credit is given per category.
Use the in-game checklist categories rather than memory: the counter is stricter than the trophy list about small one-off tasks.
The trophy pops the moment the counter first reads 100%, mid-session, with no extra turn-in.
If the counter stalls at 99%, the usual culprits are a single undiscovered location and an unfinished activity type.
Bank the strand and collectible categories before the activity quotas: they are the slowest percentages to move at the end.

trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunt events across Leonida: jumps, near-miss chains and the other stunt categories the stats screen counts. A pure volume trophy, best farmed in short sessions along stunt-dense routes.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

steps.t: Check the stats screen for your stunt total; only completed stunts count, not attempts.
Chain stunts during normal travel instead of grinding them separately: jumps and near misses stack up across the map.
Work the stunt-jump locations district by district, marking each one off as its completion registers.
In a fast car on the causeways, near-miss chains are the quickest repeatable stunt source.
The trophy pops on the 250th completed stunt, wherever it happens.
Favour stunt jumps near respawn points: a failed attempt costs seconds there, not a long drive back.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample every activity type in the game once: races, fishing, arcade, shooting range and the rest of the activity icons. Quick and easy if you try each icon the first time it appears.
trophies.name: Master of None

steps.t: Open the map legend and list the distinct activity icons; each one is a type you must try once.
Start each activity once; you only need to try it, not win or finish it, for it to register.
Story missions introduce several types for free, so check the stats count after each chapter.
The trophy pops when the last unplayed activity type is started for the first time.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.

a.t: Exophase's tracked counter for this trophy reads 42 challenges.

b.t: PowerPyx counts the same 42 range challenges and notes the unlockable expert variants are not required for the trophy.

disputes.q: Do the unlockable expert range variants count toward the trophy?

trophies.guide: Gold-medal every Shooting Range challenge — 42 of them on PlayStation's tracked counter. Learn each weapon class's target pattern, then chase golds range by range; medals save individually, so progress is never lost.
trophies.name: The Shootist

steps.t: PlayStation tracks 42 Shooting Range challenges for this trophy; finish any one to open its range's set.
Learn one weapon class at a time: gold scores are about accuracy streaks, not raw speed.
Replay a challenge immediately while its target pattern is fresh; medals are kept per challenge.
Save the moving-target and hostage-pattern challenges for last, once your aim settings feel right.
The trophy pops when the 42nd gold medal registers on the counter.
If a range's pattern keeps beating you, watch one full demonstration cycle before shooting: the order never changes.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win the Top Fun drone race at every race location on the map. The drone handling is identical everywhere, so learn the boost gates on the first course and reuse the lines.
trophies.name: Top Fun

steps.t: Find each Top Fun start point on the map; every location runs the same race format.
Win your first race slowly and cleanly: hitting every boost gate beats risky shortcuts.
Tick locations off district by district so none is missed at the end.
The trophy pops on the final location's win, when every course has a victory.

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — repeats of the same race do not stack. Work through the race icons across the state, land, sea and air, and the count takes care of itself.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

steps.t: The counter tracks distinct races won, so variety matters more than repetition.
Start with the short street races near your safehouses and move outward.
Bring a tuned car in its class; race wins are far easier in the right vehicle bracket.
The trophy pops on your 20th different race victory.
Boat and air races count toward the 20 as well; do not leave them all for the end.

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal, the fishing rival, in one of his fishing challenges. Pick his earliest challenge, learn the reeling rhythm, and his later spots get easier to read.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

steps.t: Meet Cal at a fishing spot and accept his challenge; any of his challenges counts.
Match the reel tension to the fish's runs: ease off when it fights, reel when it tires.
Land a heavier total catch than Cal's before the timer ends.
The trophy pops on the challenge results screen when your catch beats his.

trophies.guide: Finish one full arcade game at any arcade cabinet. Pick the shortest cabinet game and play it to its end screen; score does not matter.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

steps.t: Enter any arcade or bar with a playable cabinet and start a game.
Choose the shortest game on offer if you want this done quickly.
Play to the game's own end screen; quitting mid-game does not count.
The trophy pops as the cabinet returns to its attract screen.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's stranger strand by completing his final mission. Strands unlock in stages as the story advances, so keep returning to his marker between chapters.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

steps.t: Meet Andy at his stranger marker and complete his first job to open the strand.
Return after story progress when his next marker appears; strands gate on chapters.
Complete each job in the strand until only the final mission remains.
Finish the final mission; the trophy pops at its end card.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's stranger strand through to his final mission. Like the other strands, new jobs appear as chapters pass.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

steps.t: Start Kenton's strand at his first stranger marker on the coast.
Work each of his jobs as they unlock between story chapters.
Expect the strand's jobs to escalate; bring a boat-capable vehicle to the later ones.
The trophy pops when his final mission completes.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's stranger strand. This strand is flagged watch: Billy's availability narrows late in the story, so finish his jobs before the finale rather than leaving them for cleanup.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

steps.t: Start Billy's strand as soon as his marker appears; do not leave it sitting.
Complete each of his jobs promptly between chapters, ahead of other side content.
Keep a save before the finale until his final mission is done, in case his availability closes.
The trophy pops at the end of his final mission.

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.

a.t: PowerPyx counts only multi-part strands toward the eight: a stranger whose work is a single one-off job does not advance the counter.

b.t: PSNProfiles' guide counts every completed strand including single-part ones, and advises watching the counter after each ending.

disputes.q: Do single-part stranger jobs count toward the 8 strands?

trophies.guide: Complete 8 full stranger mission strands. Sources disagree on whether single-part jobs advance the counter, so finish strands end-to-end and check the counter after each one until it reads 8.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

steps.t: PlayStation tracks this trophy with a counter of 8 strands; it rises only when a strand fully ends.
Start every stranger marker you see; a strand's later jobs only appear after story progress.
Finish strands one at a time so you can watch which endings move the counter.
If the counter stalls, a started strand is unfinished somewhere: re-check each giver's marker.
The trophy pops when the counter reaches 8 completed strands.
The five named strand trophies — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone — each complete one strand toward this counter as well.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's stranger strand through his final mission. His jobs unlock across the middle chapters.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

steps.t: Meet Randy at his first marker and run his opening job.
Return between chapters as each follow-up job unlocks.
His later jobs involve moving product; a fast, discreet car makes them simpler.
The trophy pops at the end of his final mission.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's stranger strand through his final mission, another of the chapter-gated strands.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

steps.t: Start Tyrone's strand at his first stranger marker.
Complete his jobs as they appear between story missions.
Keep his strand moving alongside the others so the endings do not bunch up at the finale.
The trophy pops when his final mission completes.

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot in the state. The spots are fixed locations, mostly scenic overlooks; visit each one and use the prompt, and keep a list so the last few are easy to find.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

steps.t: Meditation spots sit at marked scenic points; the first is usually found during early exploration.
Interact with each spot and stay through the full meditation animation for it to register.
Sweep the map region by region, noting which spots you have used.
The trophy pops when the final unvisited spot is used.

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt one of the unique named animals for Bret, the hunting contact. Take his marked hunt, track the animal by its signs, and bring it down cleanly.
trophies.name: Fair Game

steps.t: Meet Bret and accept one of his unique-animal hunts from his job list.
Follow the tracks and signs in the marked area until the animal is located.
Make the kill with a clean shot so the hunt registers as complete.
Return to Bret; the trophy pops when the hunt is handed in.

trophies.guide: Complete any 3 full Collectible Card sets. Cards are scattered collectibles grouped into themed sets; finish the shortest sets first and use the collection screen to see what each set still needs.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

steps.t: PlayStation tracks completed sets, not individual cards: the counter reads 3 when you are done.
Open the collection screen and pick the sets with the fewest cards to finish first.
Sweep cards while travelling for other trophies; most sit at landmarks and interiors you visit anyway.
Trade or buy missing singles where the game allows it instead of hunting the whole map for one card.
The trophy pops when the third set is completed.
Cards catch the light at night; a night sweep of a district is the fastest way to spot the ones you missed by day.

trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK photo spots at 100 different locations. Each marked location counts once; the fastest route is to clear them district by district whenever you pass one.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

steps.t: PlayStation tracks 100 locations; each spot counts once, the first time you use it.
Spots are marked in the world and on the map once discovered; use every one you pass.
Work district by district so the endgame is a short mop-up list, not a full-map search.
Pair the sweep with the exploration trophy: most spots sit in areas The Goodtime State sends you to anyway.
The trophy pops at the 100th location.
If the map stops showing new spots, zoom in: undiscovered spots only render at closer zoom levels.

trophies.guide: Complete 50 of the game's Challenges — the short scored tasks tracked in the challenges menu. Mix quick categories (driving, combat, exploration) and the count builds fast.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

steps.t: The challenges menu tracks completions against the 50 you need.
Start with the shortest challenges in each category; many complete during normal play.
Check the menu after each session and pick off anything one attempt from done.
The trophy pops on the 50th completed challenge.
Pair challenge hunting with the stunt and race trophies: the same sessions advance both counters.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner riding along, reach a 4-star wanted level, then lose it completely and escape. Build the stars somewhere with an easy disappearance route — tunnels, alleys and the metro lines break line of sight fastest.
trophies.name: Hot Together

steps.t: Have your partner in the vehicle with you before you start; the trophy needs you together.
Commit crimes in view of police until the wanted level reaches 4 stars.
Break line of sight and hide until the search cones pass; changing vehicles helps the stars drain.
The trophy pops when the wanted level clears completely while your partner is still with you.

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops in a row with your partner, keeping a wanted level alive the whole time. Plan a tight triangle of shops, keep the car running outside each one, and never let the stars fully clear between hits.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

steps.t: PlayStation counts 3 shops robbed in one unbroken wanted stretch, with your partner present.
Pick three shops close together and scout the route before starting.
Rob the first shop, keep the wanted level up on the drive, and go straight into the second and third.
The trophy pops as the third robbery registers without the wanted level ever clearing.

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles by driving them. Every new model you enter registers once; busy car parks, dealerships and rich districts are dense with models you have not driven.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

steps.t: PlayStation tracks 100 distinct vehicles discovered; sitting in a new model is what registers it.
Early on, almost every parked car is new: sweep a couple of car parks in the first hours.
Visit dealerships and wealthy districts for the rarer models as the count slows.
The trophy pops when the 100th distinct vehicle is discovered.
Emergency and service vehicles count too: an ambulance or tow truck you have never driven is a free discovery.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Drop 5 enemies during one activation of Combat Focus, the slow-motion combat ability. Set it up in a crowded firefight: line up targets before you trigger it, and use a fast-firing weapon.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

steps.t: Unlock and charge Combat Focus through normal combat first.
Start a fight with at least five enemies in one area and let them group up.
Trigger Combat Focus and drop five enemies before the meter empties; headshots save time.
The trophy pops on the fifth takedown inside the same activation.

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.

a.t: IGN's wiki reads it as a free-roam act: any take-off from VCIA in a plane you were not scheduled to fly counts, at any point in the game.

b.t: PowerPyx ties the natural window to the VCIA Takedown aftermath, when airside access and parked aircraft are both at hand, and recommends doing it then.

disputes.q: Must the unscheduled departure happen during the VCIA Takedown mission, or any time?

trophies.guide: Take off from Vice City International Airport in a plane you were never scheduled to fly. Flagged watch: the easiest window is around the VCIA Takedown mission, when airside access is wide open, so do it then rather than hoping for a later chance.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

steps.t: The trophy asks for an unscheduled departure: a take-off from VCIA in an aircraft that is not yours.
The simplest window is during or just after VCIA Takedown, when you are already airside with planes parked nearby.
Enter a parked plane, taxi to a runway and take off; the departure registers once you are airborne.
The trophy pops as the plane leaves the ground on the unscheduled flight.

trophies.guide: A cryptic one: the description points at Rhinos — the game's tanks — and heat. Sources have not confirmed the exact trigger yet, so this guide flags it unconfirmed: the working theory is a stunt involving a tank and police heat, and it is listed here honestly rather than guessed at.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

steps.t: The description is all PlayStation gives: Rhinos are tanks, and 'hot' reads as wanted heat.
Unconfirmed: no source has yet published a verified trigger, so treat every claimed method as a rumour.
Working approach used by early hunters: take a tank, raise a wanted level, and survive in it; watch whether the trophy registers.
Re-check the sources after patches; this entry will be updated when a method is confirmed by two of them.

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store and get out without ever being detected. Go in quiet, control the room fast, and leave before any alarm state counts as detection; a suppressed approach and a parked escape car do most of the work.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

steps.t: Choose a jewelry store and park your escape vehicle at its rear exit before entering.
Enter without brandishing a weapon in view of the street; detection is about being spotted, not noise alone.
Intimidate the staff, clear the cases quickly, and leave before police arrive on scene.
The trophy pops once you are clear with the take and no detection was registered.

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape each time. Banks are the heavy end of the robbery ladder: plan an entry, a vault route and an exit vehicle for each, and let the wanted level fully clear between banks.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

steps.t: PlayStation counts 5 bank vaults robbed with a successful escape; failed escapes do not advance it.
Scout each bank first: vault position, guard pattern and the fastest street exit.
Bring your partner or crew support where the game allows it; vaults are defended.
Escape fully — stars gone — before starting the next bank so each robbery counts cleanly.
The trophy pops on the fifth completed vault escape.
Vary your approach between banks: a plan that worked once draws a faster response the second time.

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob one armored truck and escape with the take. Ambush it on a quiet stretch, crack it fast, and have a vehicle change ready for the escape.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

steps.t: Armored trucks run fixed routes; follow one until it reaches a quiet stretch of road.
Stop the truck and force the rear doors; expect armed guards.
Grab the cash, switch vehicles once to break the trail, and lose the wanted level.
The trophy pops when the escape completes with the money kept.

trophies.guide: Reveal the whole map of Leonida. Exploration registers by district and landmark; the last dark patches are usually small islands and the far coast, so finish with a boat or plane sweep of the edges.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

steps.t: The map fills in as you enter each area; check the map screen for any district still dark.
Story play reveals most of the mainland without trying.
Take a boat around the coast and islands for the patches driving never touches.
The trophy pops when the last unexplored area is revealed.
Crossing into each named region is what registers; a slow coastal pass in a plane finishes the awkward corners.

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation from every gang in the state. Each gang's operation looks different — drug labs, chop shops, fronts — so identify them all on the map first, then hit one of each.
trophies.name: Pest Control

steps.t: Learn how many gangs run operations and where each type sits; the trophy needs one robbery per gang.
Rob an operation and note which gang it belonged to before moving on.
Escape after each hit; a failed escape still teaches you the layout for the retry.
The trophy pops when the last gang's operation has been robbed.

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: A quiet moment trophy: order a cocktail at the Ocean Beach spot with the view and drink it there. Available early; it is the kind of thing most players walk past for a hundred hours.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

steps.t: Head to Ocean Beach, the strip facing the ocean on the city's east side.
Find the cocktail spot with the view the description means — a bar terrace overlooking the beach.
Order a cocktail and drink it at the spot; the trophy pops as the moment completes.

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: During the showroom set-piece, drive a car out through the showroom glass. It is tied to a story beat, so when the showroom sequence starts, get in a car inside and floor it through the window.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

steps.t: The opportunity comes in the story's vehicle-showroom sequence; watch for the interior scene.
Get into one of the showroom cars rather than leaving on foot.
Accelerate straight through the glass frontage to the street.
The trophy pops as the car lands outside; if missed, replay the mission from the story menu.

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Tied to the bowling-alley story beat at Kolt & Associates. When the sequence puts you in the alley, complete the follow-through action the scene sets up; mission replay covers a miss.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

steps.t: Reach the Kolt & Associates bowling-alley sequence in the story.
Play the scene as directed until the bowling moment arrives.
Complete the follow-through the scene asks for; the trophy pops as the scene ends.

trophies.guide: Another cryptic description, this one about the partnership — the two protagonists. No source has confirmed the trigger yet; the honest reading is a co-operative milestone with your partner, and it is flagged unconfirmed until two sources agree on what pops it.
trophies.name: Personal Best

steps.t: PlayStation's text is the only hard fact: it involves the partnership, and 'mass appeal' hints at an audience or crowd.
Unconfirmed: claimed triggers circulate, but none is verified by two sources yet.
Working approach: complete partner activities together — races, robberies and escapes as a duo — and note any that register progress.
This entry will be revised the moment a trigger is confirmed; it is not guessed at here.

a.t: Push Square's guide treats the trophy as choice-based: it pops for committing to one branch of the endgame choice, so a single playthrough is enough.

b.t: Game8's list reads it as cumulative: the trophy tracks major choices across the whole story, not one decision, and warns against skipping early choice scenes.

disputes.q: Does this trophy hinge on one endgame choice, or on choices across the story?

trophies.guide: The list's one genuinely missable trophy: it turns on story choices. Keep manual saves before every major choice from Chapter 4 on, commit to your branch, and the pre-finale save covers you if the other branch is ever needed.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

steps.t: From Chapter 4 onward, save manually before any story choice the game presents as major.
Play your chosen branch through; the trophy is tied to the choices themselves, not to a 'right' answer.
Sources disagree on whether one endgame choice or the whole run of choices matters, so miss none of the choice scenes.
The trophy pops when the qualifying choice sequence resolves in the endgame.

trophies.guide: Cryptic and unconfirmed: 'second time's the charm' points at failing or missing something once and succeeding on the retry. No verified trigger exists yet, so this is flagged honestly; the leading theory is a mission or activity failed once, then completed.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

steps.t: The description implies a failure followed by a success at the same thing.
Unconfirmed: no two sources agree on a verified trigger at the time of writing.
Working approach: when an activity or mission attempt fails, retry it immediately rather than moving on, and note any pop.
This guide will name the trigger once a source confirms it; until then it stays flagged, not faked.

trophies.guide: The strangest description on the list, and unconfirmed by every source so far. It reads as a scripted surprise event somewhere in Leonida; hunters are pointed at the state's odd corners, but nothing is verified, and this entry says so instead of inventing a location.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

steps.t: PlayStation offers nothing beyond the reaction in the description: something strange happens.
Unconfirmed: rumoured locations circulate in forums, none verified by two sources.
Working approach: explore the state's remote and odd locations during the exploration sweep, and investigate any scripted oddity you trigger.
When a trigger is confirmed by two sources, this entry will be rewritten with it; for now it is an honest unknown.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Hit pedestrians with a melee attack from a moving vehicle — a drive-by swing, bowling them over. Slow passes along a busy pavement with the melee button timed as you pass do it safely and quickly.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

steps.t: You need a vehicle, a melee swing from the driver's seat, and pedestrians in reach.
Drive slowly along a crowded pavement so the swing can connect without a crash.
Time the melee press as a pedestrian passes the window; contact is what counts.
The trophy pops on the connecting hit.

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder a cumulative $250,000 of Marked Bills through your laundering contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies and heists; run them through contacts regularly instead of hoarding, and the total climbs steadily.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

steps.t: PlayStation tracks the laundered total against $250,000; only bills passed through contacts count.
Collect Marked Bills from robberies, heists and operations as you play the rest of the list.
Visit laundering contacts whenever your marked-bill stock is high; do not sit on them.
The trophy pops when the cumulative laundered amount crosses $250,000.
Laundering takes a cut, so the marked bills you collect need to total more than the $250,000 target.

trophies.guide: Spend a cumulative $100,000 in shops — clothes, weapons, vehicles services, food, anything with a till. It accumulates across the whole game, so normal play plus a late shopping spree finishes it.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

steps.t: PlayStation tracks total shop spending against $100,000, across every shop type.
Buy your weapons, ammo, armour and outfits rather than scavenging; it all counts.
If you are short late, vehicle customisation is the fastest honest way to spend.
The trophy pops when the spending total crosses $100,000.
Property purchases do not count here — this counter watches shop tills only, so keep the garage fund separate.

trophies.guide: Buy every garage property on the map. Garages are bought at their for-sale signs; sweep the property listings, save heist money for the expensive ones, and buy them all — owning them also feeds the vehicle trophies.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

steps.t: Garage properties are listed on the map and property sites once you can afford property.
Buy the cheap garages first with early heist money; they start paying for themselves in storage value.
Keep a fund untouched for the most expensive garage instead of spending down to zero.
The trophy pops when the final unowned garage is purchased.
Each garage's storage also makes the 100-vehicle discovery trophy far easier to finish.

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Any vehicle you own or keep can be registered at the app; register your regular rides first, then fill the remaining slots with cheap buys.
trophies.name: On the Spot

steps.t: PlayStation counts 10 vehicles registered to the app; registrations are permanent once made.
Open the Scooter Bros app and register the vehicles you already own or store.
Buy or keep extra cheap vehicles until the registered count reaches ten.
The trophy pops on the tenth registration.
